For hosted, we support Redwood-managed KMS by default but there is an integration path for customer KMS for Private deployments. On logs: we provide detailed request traces in the console and can stream raw audit events to your syslog or S3 for up to 90 days as an add-on.

[02:20] Ravi Patel: yes we can. I want to call out that the KV cache warmup was the big factor in the 95th percentile spikes last time — the model variant and the quant profile matter a lot for these long sessions.

[02:35] [02:35] Speaker 2 (transcription noise): mm-hmm

[02:40] Sara Delgado: Can you remind us how the automatic prefix caching works again? We saw some cache misses in staging when multiple parallel sessions started cold.

[02:51] Ravi Patel: Sure. Redwood's runtime does prefix/KV caching per sequence prefix and also maintains an LRU for cache entries. When you have many parallel users with different conversation prefixes, the cache hit rate drops and we fall back to more computation which increases tail latency. For this pilot, we recommended a small warmup traffic pattern to populate prefix entries — e.g., run 50 synthetic sessions that cover your top 20 prompt templates before launching heavy tests.

[03:18] Tom Nguyen: ok that's useful. Is there a config to pin caching to dedicated nodes? We saw eviction when autoscaling kicked in.

[03:28] Ravi Patel: On Dedicated you can configure sticky routing to a pool and pin certain workload keys so the same worker keeps the KV. There's also a recommended autoscale window — avoid very short-lived scale-in intervals under high concurrency. I'll add the recommended config to the bench spreadsheet.

[03:45] Maya Chen: quick interjection — we noticed another hiccup: staging API gateway returned intermittent 502s when prefix sizes exceeded 8k tokens; could be a timeout on the gateway vs runtime. Tom, do you have the gateway config?

[03:58] Tom Nguyen: we have 30s backend timeout currently. Some of the long sessions took longer, maybe we need to bump to 90s for staging. We'll try 60s first and monitor.

[04:12] Priya Kapoor: On data residency: our legal team insists no logs cross the EU boundary for EU patients. Can we route EU traffic to the EU region and ensure data at rest is pinned?

[04:22] Ravi Patel: Yes — regional routing policy can pin requests by country IP or token attribute. For Private deployments we can ensure data at rest is localized; for Hosted API we have EU regions and can route. We'll produce a diagram in the security doc.

Results summary: tail latency for long sessions degraded significantly when cache hit rates dropped below ~55%. Median latency for long sessions with high hit-rate was 450ms per call (per token step was averaged) — when hit rate dropped median jumped to ~1.2s and 95th crossed 4s in some runs.

[05:44] Ravi Patel: I used our bench harness with template substitution to mimic back-and-forth turns and included stop sequences similar to your transcripts. We can run the bench on a non-quant profile if you want to compare.
